f.title: Conduct a post-authorisation safety study (PASS) when the Agency imposes one after authorisation
f.statement: After the granting of a marketing authorisation, the Agency may impose an obligation on the marketing authorisation holder to conduct a post-authorisation safety study if there are concerns about the risks of an authorised medicinal product. If the same concerns apply to more than one medicinal product, the Agency shall, following consultation with the Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee, encourage the marketing authorisation holders concerned to conduct a joint post-authorisation safety study.
f.clause: Article 1 point 4 - inserted Article 10a(1)(a) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004
f.applicability: Centrally authorised medicinal products for human use, where the Agency imposes the obligation after authorisation because of concerns about the risks
f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Risk management & minimisation

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (European Medicines Agency imposes the obligation)
rows.location: Article 1 point 4 - inserted Article 10a(1)(a) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

Statement unchanged. Double-check: quote proves the Agency power and the joint-PASS encouragement; Mandatory for the MAH is a judgement-call level (source says the Agency 'may impose'), so below 90.

f.title: Conduct a post-authorisation efficacy study (PAES) when the Agency imposes one, within the notified timeframe
f.statement: After the granting of a marketing authorisation, the Agency may impose an obligation on the marketing authorisation holder to conduct a post-authorisation efficacy study when the understanding of the disease or the clinical methodology indicate that previous efficacy evaluations might have to be revised significantly; the obligation shall be based on the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 10b, taking into account the scientific guidance referred to in Article 108a of Directive 2001/83/EC. The imposition of such an obligation shall be duly justified, notified in writing, and shall include the objectives and timeframe for submission and conduct of the study.
f.clause: Article 1 point 4 - inserted Article 10a(1)(b) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004
f.legal_basis: Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Art 10a(1)(b), Art 10b; Directive 2001/83/EC Art 108a
f.applicability: Centrally authorised medicinal products for human use, where the Agency imposes the obligation after authorisation

f.title: Request opportunity to present written observations on an imposed PASS/PAES within 30 days
f.statement: The Agency shall provide the marketing authorisation holder with an opportunity to present written observations in response to the imposition of the study obligation within a time limit which it shall specify, if the marketing authorisation holder so requests within 30 days of receipt of the written notification of the obligation.
f.clause: Article 1 point 4 - inserted Article 10a(2) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

f.title: Update the risk management system when the Commission confirms an imposed PASS/PAES as an MA condition
f.statement: On the basis of the written observations submitted by the marketing authorisation holder, and of the opinion of the Agency, the Commission shall withdraw or confirm the obligation. Where the Commission confirms the obligation, the marketing authorisation shall be varied to include the obligation as a condition of the marketing authorisation and the risk management system shall be updated accordingly.
f.clause: Article 1 point 4 - inserted Article 10a(3) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Epidemiology / safety studies

f.title: Submit consolidated renewal file including ADR and PSUR evaluation at least 9 months before expiry
f.statement: For renewal, the marketing authorisation holder shall provide the Agency with a consolidated version of the file in respect of quality, safety and efficacy, including the evaluation of data contained in suspected adverse reactions reports and periodic safety update reports submitted in accordance with Chapter 3, and information on all variations introduced since the marketing authorisation was granted, at least 9 months before the marketing authorisation ceases to be valid in accordance with paragraph 1.

f.title: Undergo one additional five-year renewal if the Commission so decides on pharmacovigilance grounds
f.statement: Once renewed, the marketing authorisation shall be valid for an unlimited period, unless the Commission decides, on justified grounds relating to pharmacovigilance, including exposure of an insufficient number of patients to the medicinal product concerned, to proceed with one additional five-year renewal in accordance with paragraph 2.
f.clause: Article 1 point 5(b) - Article 14(3) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

f.title: Comply with specific safety and incident-notification conditions of an authorisation under exceptional circumstances (reassessed annually)
f.statement: In exceptional circumstances and following consultation with the applicant, the marketing authorisation may be granted subject to certain conditions, in particular relating to the safety of the medicinal product, notification to the competent authorities of any incident relating to its use, and action to be taken. It may be granted only when the applicant can show that he is unable to provide comprehensive data on efficacy and safety under normal conditions of use, for objective, verifiable reasons, and must be based on one of the grounds in Annex I to Directive 2001/83/EC. Continuation of the marketing authorisation shall be linked to the annual reassessment of these conditions.
f.clause: Article 1 point 5(c) - Article 14(8) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004
f.legal_basis: Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Art 14(8); Directive 2001/83/EC Annex I
f.applicability: Marketing authorisations granted under exceptional circumstances

f.title: Incorporate marketing authorisation conditions in the risk management system
f.statement: The marketing authorisation holder shall incorporate any conditions referred to in points (c), (ca), (cb) and (cc) of Article 9(4) or in Article 10a, or in Article 14(7) and (8) in his risk management system.
f.clause: Article 1 point 6 - inserted Article 14a of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

f.title: Introduce manufacturing/control changes reflecting scientific and technical progress and apply for the variations
f.statement: After a marketing authorisation has been granted in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 726/2004, the marketing authorisation holder shall, in respect of the methods of manufacture and control provided for in points (d) and (h) of Article 8(3) of Directive 2001/83/EC, take account of scientific and technical progress and introduce any changes that may be required to enable the medicinal product to be manufactured and checked by means of generally accepted scientific methods. He shall apply for approval of corresponding variations in accordance with the Regulation.
f.clause: Article 1 point 7 - Article 16(1) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004
f.applicability: Centrally authorised medicinal products for human use

f.title: Forthwith provide new information that might require amending the dossier, SmPC or conditions
f.statement: The marketing authorisation holder shall forthwith provide the Agency, the Commission and the Member States with any new information which might entail the amendment of the particulars or documents referred to in Article 8(3), Article 10, 10a, 10b and 11, or Article 32(5) of Directive 2001/83/EC, in Annex I thereto, or in Article 9(4) of this Regulation.

f.title: Forthwith inform of foreign prohibitions or restrictions and any new benefit-risk information
f.statement: The marketing authorisation holder shall forthwith inform the Agency and the Commission of any prohibition or restriction imposed by the competent authorities of any country in which the medicinal product is marketed and of any other new information which might influence the evaluation of the benefits and risks of the medicinal product concerned. The information shall include both positive and negative results of clinical trials or other studies in all indications and populations, whether or not included in the marketing authorisation, as well as data on the use of the medicinal product where such use is outside the terms of the marketing authorisation.
f.clause: Article 1 point 7 - Article 16(2), second subparagraph, of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

f.title: Keep product information up to date with current scientific knowledge and published assessment outcomes
f.statement: The marketing authorisation holder shall ensure that the product information is kept up to date with the current scientific knowledge including the conclusions of the assessment and recommendations made public by means of the European medicines web-portal established in accordance with Article 26.
f.clause: Article 1 point 7 - Article 16(3) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

f.title: Answer fully and promptly any Agency request for data showing the benefit-risk balance remains favourable
f.statement: In order to be able to continuously assess the risk-benefit balance, the Agency may at any time ask the marketing authorisation holder to forward data demonstrating that the risk-benefit balance remains favourable. The marketing authorisation holder shall answer fully and promptly any such request.
f.clause: Article 1 point 7 - Article 16(4), first subparagraph, of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

f.title: Submit a copy of the PSMF to the Agency within 7 days of request
f.statement: The Agency may at any time ask the marketing authorisation holder to submit a copy of the pharmacovigilance system master file. The marketing authorisation holder shall submit the copy at the latest 7 days after receipt of the request.

f.title: Be subject to verification and possible pre-authorisation inspection of the PV system by the PV supervisory authority
f.statement: The supervisory authorities for pharmacovigilance shall be responsible for verifying on behalf of the Union that the marketing authorisation holder satisfies the pharmacovigilance requirements laid down in Titles IX and XI of Directive 2001/83/EC. They may, if considered necessary, conduct pre-authorisation inspections to verify the accuracy and successful implementation of the pharmacovigilance system as described by the applicant in support of his application.
f.clause: Article 1 point 9(a) - Article 19(1), second subparagraph, of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004
f.legal_basis: Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 Art 19(1); Directive 2001/83/EC Titles IX and XI

f.title: Apply the MAH pharmacovigilance obligations of Directive 2001/83/EC Article 104 to centrally authorised products
f.statement: The obligations of marketing authorisation holders laid down in Article 104 of Directive 2001/83/EC shall apply to marketing authorisation holders for medicinal products for human use authorised in accordance with this Regulation.
f.clause: Article 1 point 11 - Article 21(1), first subparagraph, of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

f.title: MAs granted before 2 July 2012 need not operate an RMS for each product unless one is imposed
f.statement: Without prejudice to paragraphs 2, 3 and 4 of Article 21, holders of marketing authorisations granted before 2 July 2012 shall, by way of derogation from Article 104(3)(c) of Directive 2001/83/EC, not be required to operate a risk management system for each medicinal product.

f.title: Submit a detailed RMS description when the Agency imposes a risk management system obligation
f.statement: The Agency may impose an obligation on a marketing authorisation holder to operate a risk management system, as referred to in point (c) of Article 104(3) of Directive 2001/83/EC, if there are concerns about the risks affecting the risk-benefit balance of an authorised medicinal product. In that context, the Agency shall also oblige the marketing authorisation holder to submit a detailed description of the risk-management system which he intends to introduce. The imposition shall be duly justified, notified in writing, and shall include the timeframe for submission of the detailed description.
f.clause: Article 1 point 11 - Article 21(2) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

In that context, the Agency shall also oblige the marketing authorisation holder to submit a detailed description of the risk-management system which he intends to introduce for the medicinal product concerned.

f.statement: The Agency shall provide the marketing authorisation holder with an opportunity to present written observations in response to the imposition of the risk management system obligation within a time limit which it shall specify, if the marketing authorisation holder so requests within 30 days of receipt of the written notification of the obligation. f.title: Apply Directive Article 106a(1) safety-announcement obligations to centrally authorised products
f.statement: The obligations of marketing authorisation holders laid down in Article 106a(1) of Directive 2001/83/EC shall apply to the safety announcements referred to in point (e) of Article 57(1) of this Regulation concerning medicinal products for human use authorised in accordance with this Regulation.

f.title: Include the additional monitoring statement and black symbol in the SmPC and package leaflet
f.statement: For medicinal products included in the additional monitoring list, the summary of product characteristics and the package leaflet shall include the statement "This medicinal product is subject to additional monitoring". That statement shall be preceded by a black symbol selected by the Commission following a recommendation of the Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee by 2 January 2012, and shall be followed by an appropriate standardised explanatory sentence.

f.title: Record and report suspected adverse reactions per Directive Articles 107 and 107a for centrally authorised products
f.statement: The obligations of marketing authorisation holders and of Member States laid down in Articles 107 and 107a of Directive 2001/83/EC shall apply to the recording and reporting of suspected adverse reactions for medicinal products for human use authorised in accordance with this Regulation.
f.clause: Article 1 point 11 - Article 28(1) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

rows.quote: 1.   The obligations of marketing authorisation holders and of Member States laid down in Articles 107 and 107a of Directive 2001/83/EC shall apply to the recording and reporting of suspected adverse reactions for medicinal products for human use authorised in accordance with this Regulation.
rows.location: Article 1 point 11 - Article 28(1) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004
rows.review_note: Review: RACI accountable governance-3 -> governance-1 (QPPV oversight of ICSR/PSUR/emerging-risk duties). Double-check: quote proves the cross-application of Directive Arts 107 and 107a. Confirmed.

f.title: Submit PSURs per Directive Article 107b and Union reference date procedures for centrally authorised products
f.statement: The obligations of marketing authorisation holders laid down in Article 107b of Directive 2001/83/EC and the procedures under Articles 107b and 107c of that Directive shall apply to the submission of periodic safety update reports, the establishment of Union reference dates and changes to the frequency of submission of periodic safety update reports for medicinal products for human use authorised in accordance with this Regulation.
f.clause: Article 1 point 11 - Article 28(2), first subparagraph, of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

rows.quote: 2.   The obligations of marketing authorisation holders laid down in Article 107b of Directive 2001/83/EC and the procedures under Article 107b and Article 107c of that Directive shall apply to the submission of periodic safety update reports, the establishment of Union reference dates and changes to the frequency of submission of periodic safety update reports for medicinal products for human use authorised in accordance with this Regulation.
rows.location: Article 1 point 11 - Article 28(2), first subparagraph, of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004
rows.review_note: Review: RACI accountable governance-3 -> governance-1 (QPPV oversight of ICSR/PSUR/emerging-risk duties). Double-check: quote proves the cross-application of Directive Arts 107b/107c. Confirmed.

f.title: Pre-2 July 2012 MAs without PSUR frequency conditions follow the transitional PSUR schedule of Article 107c(2)
f.statement: The provisions applicable to the submission of periodic safety update reports laid down in the second subparagraph of Article 107c(2) of Directive 2001/83/EC shall apply to holders of marketing authorisations granted before 2 July 2012 whose PSUR frequency and dates of submission are not laid down as a condition to the marketing authorisation, until another frequency or other dates are laid down in the marketing authorisation or determined in accordance with Article 107c of that Directive.
f.clause: Article 1 point 11 - Article 28(2), second subparagraph, of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004
f.applicability: Marketing authorisations granted before 2 July 2012 without PSUR frequency/dates as an MA condition

rows.quote: The provisions applicable to the submission of periodic safety update reports laid down in the second subparagraph of Article 107c(2) of that Directive shall apply to holders of marketing authorisations which were granted before 2 July 2012 and for which the frequency and dates of submission of the periodic safety update reports are not laid down as a condition to the marketing authorisation until such time as another frequency or other dates of submission of the reports are laid down in the marketing authorisation or are determined in accordance with Article 107c of that Directive.
rows.location: Article 1 point 11 - Article 28(2), second subparagraph, of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004
rows.review_note: Review: RACI accountable governance-3 -> governance-1 (QPPV oversight of ICSR/PSUR/emerging-risk duties). Double-check: quote proves the transitional PSUR schedule for pre-2 July 2012 MAs. Confirmed.

f.title: Comment on the PSUR assessment report within 30 days of receipt
f.statement: The rapporteur shall prepare an assessment report within 60 days of receipt of the periodic safety update report and send it to the Agency and to PRAC members; the Agency shall send the report to the marketing authorisation holder. Within 30 days of receipt of the assessment report, the marketing authorisation holder and the members of the Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee may submit comments to the Agency and to the rapporteur.
f.clause: Article 1 point 11 - Article 28(3), second and third subparagraphs, of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

f.title: Inform the Agency and national competent authorities when new or changed risks or benefit-risk changes are detected
f.statement: The Agency and national competent authorities and the marketing authorisation holder shall inform each other in the event of new risks or risks that have changed or changes to the risk-benefit balance being detected.
f.clause: Article 1 point 11 - Article 28a(3) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder, European Medicines Agency and national competent authorities
rows.quote: 3.   The Agency and national competent authorities and the marketing authorisation holder shall inform each other in the event of new risks or risks that have changed or changes to the risk-benefit balance being detected.

rows.review_note: Review: RACI accountable governance-3 -> governance-1 (QPPV oversight of ICSR/PSUR/emerging-risk duties). Double-check: quote proves the mutual information duty for all three actors. Confirmed.

f.title: Follow the Directive PASS procedure for imposed non-interventional PASS of centrally authorised products
f.statement: For non-interventional post-authorisation safety studies concerning centrally authorised medicinal products for human use which fulfil one of the requirements referred to in Articles 10 and 10a of this Regulation, the procedure provided for in paragraphs 3 to 7 of Article 107m, Articles 107n to 107p and Article 107q(1) of Directive 2001/83/EC shall apply.
f.clause: Article 1 point 11 - Article 28b(1) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004
f.applicability: Non-interventional PASS imposed as conditions under Articles 10 or 10a

rows.quote: 1.   For non-interventional post-authorisation safety studies concerning medicinal products for human use authorised in accordance with this Regulation which fulfil one of the requirements referred to in Articles 10 and 10a of this Regulation, the procedure provided for in paragraphs 3 to 7 of Article 107m, Articles 107n to 107p and Article 107q(1) of Directive 2001/83/EC shall apply.
rows.location: Article 1 point 11 - Article 28b(1) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

f.title: Electronically submit information on all authorised medicinal products to the Agency by 2 July 2012
f.statement: For the purposes of the Article 57 database, marketing authorisation holders shall, by 2 July 2012 at the latest, electronically submit to the Agency information on all medicinal products for human use authorised or registered in the Union, using the format made public by the Agency.
f.clause: Article 1 point 13(b) - Article 57(2), second subparagraph point (b), of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004
f.applicability: All medicinal products for human use authorised or registered in the Union

rows.quote: marketing authorisation holders shall, by 2 July 2012 at the latest, electronically submit to the Agency information on all medicinal products for human use authorised or registered in the Union, using the format referred to in point (a);

rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote lacks its lead-in ('For the purposes of the database...') and refers to 'the format referred to in point (a)', which the statement renders as the format made public by the Agency; below 90.

f.title: Inform the Agency of any new or varied marketing authorisations in the Union using the electronic format
f.statement: From 2 July 2012, marketing authorisation holders shall inform the Agency of any new or varied marketing authorisations granted in the Union, using the format made public by the Agency.
f.clause: Article 1 point 13(b) - Article 57(2), second subparagraph point (c), of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

rows.quote: from the date set out in point (b), marketing authorisation holders shall inform the Agency of any new or varied marketing authorisations granted in the Union, using the format referred to in point (a).

rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote says 'from the date set out in point (b)'; the 2 July 2012 date and format description come from outside the quote; below 90.

f.title: PSMF obligation for MAs granted before 2 July 2012 applies from renewal or 3 years after 2 July 2012, whichever is earlier
f.statement: The obligation on the marketing authorisation holder to maintain and make available on request a pharmacovigilance system master file (Article 104(3)(b) of Directive 2001/83/EC as amended by Directive 2010/84/EU), which applies to centrally authorised products by virtue of Article 21 of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004, shall apply to marketing authorisations granted before 2 July 2012 as from either the date on which those marketing authorisations are renewed, or the expiry of a period of 3 years starting from 2 July 2012, whichever is the earlier.
f.clause: Article 3(1) Transitional provisions

rows.deadline: From renewal of the MA or expiry of 3 years from 2 July 2012, whichever is earlier
rows.quote:
1.   The obligation on the part of the marketing authorisation holder to maintain and make available on request a pharmacovigilance system master file in respect of one or more medicinal products for human use provided for in Article 104(3)(b) of Directive 2001/83/EC as amended by Directive 2010/84/EU, which applies to medicinal products for human use authorised pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 by virtue of Article 21 of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 as amended by this Regulation, shall apply to marketing authorisations granted before 2 July 2012 as from either:

 (a)

 the date on which those marketing authorisations are renewed; or

 (b)

 the expiry of a period of 3 years starting from 2 July 2012,

 whichever is the earlier.
rows.location: Article 3(1) Transitional provisions
rows.review_note: Review: RACI accountable governance-3 -> governance-1 (QPPV oversees PSMF). Double-check: quote proves the transitional PSMF application dates. Confirmed.

f.title: Directive PASS procedure applies only to studies commenced after 2 July 2012
f.statement: The procedure provided for in Articles 107m to 107q of Directive 2001/83/EC as amended by Directive 2010/84/EU, which apply by virtue of Article 28b of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004, shall apply only to studies which have commenced after 2 July 2012.
f.clause: Article 3(2) Transitional provisions
